concept: An acid is neutralised when the alkali added matches it, and the pH jumps at that point.
goal: Find the volume of alkali at which the acid is neutralised by watching the colour and the pH.
phenomenon: A burette holds alkali above a flask of acid with indicator. Drops fall into the flask, the liquid swirls, the colour changes near the end point and the pH climbs steeply.

interactions.target: down to open the tap a little at a time
interactions.response: drops fall into the flask and the liquid level in the burette drops

scene.apparatus: a burette above a flask of acid on a white tile
fills: a white tile behind the flask
scene.wideScreen: The pH meter dial and a pH against volume graph stand beside the burette.

motion: Drops fall, the liquid swirls, and the colour fades in as the end point nears. Under reduced motion the flask changes colour without the swirl.
science: pH against volume added: computed by model code with a steep rise at the end point

expectedBehaviour.text: the pH rises as more alkali is added

predict.question: Will the pH change slowly and evenly as alkali is added?
choices: No, it jumps near the end point
predict.check: Open the tap a little at a time and watch the pH dial near 25 cm3.

steps: Drag the burette tap lever down a little and watch the first drops.
Keep adding until the colour begins to change.
Add single drops past the end point and read the pH.
